The State Represented By The Special ... vs B.Narasimha, on 4
October, 2024
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.290 of 2016
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer and Sri N.Narasimha Murthy, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer aggrieved by the order and decree dated 19.12.2015 passed in LAOP.No.853 of 2012 on the file of the II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court').
3.

entities.text: II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In brief, the facts of the case are that the lands admeasuring 2,297 square yards situated in Sy.No.114 of Laxmiguda Village, Rajendranagar Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, belonging to the respondents/claimants were acquired for development of P7 road from Mailardevally to Srisailam road via Jalpally; that Draft Notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published in A.P. 2 AKS, J & LNA, J Gazette on 21.04.2007; and that after following the procedure prescribed under the Act and after conducting enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer passed an Award, dated 24.08.2009,
fixing the market value of the acquired lands @ Rs.40,00,000/- per acre.
4.

Not being satisfied with the Award, the respondents/ claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was referred to the competent civil court and numbered as L.A.O.P.No.853 of 2012 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-12 were marked.
On behalf of the appellant-Referring Officer, R.W-1 was examined and Ex.B-1-Award was marked.

6. On due appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Reference Court enhanced the market value of the acquired lands to Rs.1,200/- per square yard, apart from granting other statutory benefits under the Act to the respondents/claimants.
Aggrieved thereby, the present appeal is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

sentences.text: Learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer contended that the Reference Court erred in awarding compensation on acreage basis when vast extent of Acs.1.02 guntas was acquired, which includes the subject land belonging to the respondents/claimants; that the Reference Court has erred in placing reliance on the orders passed in LAOP.No.515 of 2008 and thereby, enhancing the compensation based on the said orders; that the Reference Court has not properly appreciated the documentary evidence adduced before it; and that therefore, the impugned order is irregular and contrary to law and accordingly, the same is liable to be set aside.

8. Learned counsel for the respondents-claimants contended that the Reference Court has appreciated the voluminous evidence adduced by the respondents/claimant in support of their claim for enhancement of compensation in correct perspective and on finding that the respondents/claimants were able to establish their claim by adducing cogent evidence to that effect,
rightly enhanced the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer and passed the impugned order fixing market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis.

Therefore, the impugned order passed by the 4 AKS, J & LNA, J Reference Court is based on proper appreciation of facts of the case and the evidence adduced before it and as such, the same needs no interference by this Court.

9. The respondents/claimants to substantiate their claim for enhancement of market value of the acquired lands have adduced and got marked as many as 12 exhibits, i.e., Exs.A-1 to A-12, which include Exs.A-1 to A-3, A-6 and A-7-the Market Value Certificates issued by the Sub-Registrar Offices concerned.

The issue as to whether the Market Value Certificates can form the basis for determining the market value of the acquired land has been dealt with by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of judgments, i.e., in BSNL Vs. Nemichand Damodardas1 and Choda Dharampal Reddy Vs. Revenue Divisional Officer, Nalgonda District2, wherein it is held as under:-
"There may be

entities.text: Choda Dharampal Reddy Vs. Revenue Divisional Officer, Nalgonda District2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: various factors, which are required to be considered for determining the market value of the land.

The market value of the land depends upon the location of the land; area of the land; whether the land is in a developed area or not; whether the acquisition is of a small plot of land or a big chunk of land and number of (2022)
14 SCC 60 1998(1) ALD 261 (DB) 5 AKS, J & LNA, J other advantageous and disadvantageous factors are required to be considered.
Therefore, there cannot be the same market value for the different lands while determining the compensation for the lands acquired under the Land Acquisition Act.

Therefore, the rates mentioned in the Ready Reckoner, which are basically for the purpose of collection of stamp duty and as observed hereinabove, which are the uniform rates for all the lands in the area, cannot be the basis for determination of the compensation for the lands acquired under the Land Acquisition Act.

" 
10. In view of the aforesaid proposition laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it can be safely held that Exs.A-1 to A-3, A-6 and A-7-Market Value Certificates cannot form basis for determination The State Represented By The Special ... vs B.Narasimha, on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68084971/
2 of market value of the acquired property and therefore, the same cannot be looked into.
11. Ex.A-4 is the proceedings of the Collector, Ex.A-5 is the notice of Award and Ex.A-8 is the tax demand notice.
From the said documents, no clue can be taken for fixation of market value of the subject acquired lands and hence, the same cannot be considered.
6 AKS, J & LNA, J 12.
Exs.A-10 and A-12 are the sale deeds, dated 07.06.2007 and 02.01.2011, respectively, i.e., they relate to post-notification and hence, they are not considered.

13. Ex.A-11 is sale deed dated 02.02.2007, whereunder the land covered therein situated in Laxmiguda Village was sold @ Rs.1,200/- per square yard.
14.
The respondents/claimants mainly relied on Ex.A-9-order dated 20.11.2013, passed by the Reference Court in LAOP.No.515 of 2008.
The subject lands covered in the said O.P. which are situated in Sy.No.96 of Laxmiguda Village were also acquired by the Government for development of P7 road from Mailardevpally to Srisailam Road.
15. Thus, the location and the purpose of acquisition of the subject acquired lands and the lands covered in O.P.No.515 of 2008 are same/identical.
16. Therefore, the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. v. State of Jammu and Kashmir3 is squarely applicable to the present case.

entities.text: Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. v. State of Jammu and Kashmir3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said judgment, it is held as under:-
(2017) 4 SCC 717 7 AKS, J & LNA, J "When the lands are more or less situated nearby and when the acquired lands are identical and similar and the acquisition is for the same purpose, it would not be proper to discriminate between the landowners unless there are strong reasons."
17.

In the light of the above judgment, since the subject acquired lands are situated nearby to the lands covered under Ex.A-9 and the purpose of acquisition in both the cases is same and further,
since both the lands fall in the same alignment and also, in order to maintain parity, this Court feels that it would not be proper to discriminate in fixation of market value of acquired lands.
18.

Even the market value of Rs.1,200/- per square yard that is reflected in Ex.A-11-sale deed,
remained unrebutted by the Land Acquisition Officer.

19. As regards the contention of the learned Government Pleader for Appeals regarding fixation of market value of the acquired lands on acreage basis instead of yardage basis as observed by the Reference Court, it is discernable from record that in the instant case, an extent of 2,297 square yards of lands were acquired, which shows that the said land was being used for other than agricultural 8 AKS, J & LNA, J purposes, therefore, the respondents/claimants are entitled to The State Represented By The Special ... vs B.Narasimha, on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68084971/
3 compensation for the acquired lands on yardage basis.

entities.text: State Represented By The Special ... vs B.Narasimha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
20. In the light of the above discussion, this Court holds that the impugned order passed by the Reference Court is based on the evidence placed on record and the Reference Court has not committed any illegality or irregularity in enhancing the market value of the acquired lands to Rs.1,200/- per square yard.
21.
Therefore, this Appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.
No costs.
22. As a sequel, interim order dated 20.10.2016 passed in LAASMP.No.1012 of 2016 stands vacated.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
